item_verdicts.manifest: read; it declares status complete with commits 1987e648 and 1f1bac86, records the gate as 7 passed EXIT=0 and the negative control as 0 passed 1 failed EXIT=1, and both cited logs resolve to files I opened; it records no baseline_suite/after_suite arm.

justifications.durability: the per-round regression is guarded by test_a_new_round_starts_its_attempt_count_at_one, which seeds an earlier round's two attempts and asserts the new round's first resume records attempt 1; the negative control proves that case fails on a return to the prior formula (assert 3 == 1), so a regression in the keying is caught. The case is deterministic (temporary config home and repo, a fixed earlier-round id, no date-derived literal). Docked one because the case stubs recovery._opened_repair_rounds open, so the interaction between a new round's fresh attempt count and the run-wide one-round cap is not itself exercised.
justifications.evidence: the focused gate reproduces independently at head 1f1bac86: I ran the file with the reviewed worktree's recovery.py as the imported module (module.__file__ printed from that tree) and got 7 passed, EXIT=0 (reviewer-gate.log). The declared negative control reproduces in a scratch copy of the reviewed tree: reverting the keying to the prior formula int(prior.get("attempt") or 0) + 1 reddens the new case with assert 3 == 1, 1 failed, EXIT=1 (reviewer-negative-control.log). Both logs end with a bare EXIT= line. Deduction: the reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm, so no base/head population comparison was taken for this run — its own done-when scoped the gate to the named test file and left the wider population to a merge-time suite, so the added-failure count is unmeasured rather than zero.
justifications.fit: the change reuses the module's existing idioms — the same round-id comparison the retry cap already makes against durable.get(REPAIR_DISPATCH_FIELD) — adds locals named by mechanism (prior, same_round, attempt), updates the docstring to state why the count belongs to the round, and introduces no plan, phase, ticket or version label in names, comments or docstrings.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's goal is that the reflex count a repair round's resume attempts per round rather than across rounds, and reckon/crew/recovery.py:1913-1919 now does exactly that: _record_repair_dispatch reads prior = pointer["repair_dispatch"], computes same_round = str(prior.get("round_id") or "") == str(round_id or ""), and sets attempt = int(prior.get("attempt") or 0) + 1 if same_round else 1, so a write for a round the pointer did not last carry starts at 1 whatever an earlier round recorded. The within-round retry cap at recovery.py:2387-2391 already gated its own prior read on the same round-id comparison, so it now reads a figure belonging to the round it bounds, and the run-wide one-round-per-run cap (the opened_rounds count/round_id comparison at recovery.py:2188-2198) is untouched. The value returned by _record_repair_dispatch is the recorded attempt, and the resume path at recovery.py:2440-2453 returns it as "attempt".
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --numstat 29560d96633faf84024d625290af205f97125fa1 1f1bac86a52b7c1a846a44165873f157b43afa50 lists exactly three files — reckon/crew/recovery.py (+12/-4), tests/test_the_reflex_resumes_an_unpromoted_run.py (+44), and docs/evidence/fragments/a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk/resume-attempts-count-per-round.html (+31) — every one inside the four declared write paths; the declared figures directory was touched by nothing, and the reviewed worktree is clean at head.
